description: Re-points (SPEC §8.2.9, 0.4.0). repoint_id = SHA-256(canonical({v:1, claim: claim_id, prev, outpoint, nonce})). A reader takes re-points only from the address's state (a listing signed by a bound key). The list is one chain in order, at most 16: the first prev is the claim's outpoint, each later prev the outpoint before it; a list that does not chain, or has more than 16, is dropped before any read. The reader follows it from the claim's own coin; each valid link moves the claim, and the first link that is not valid ends the chain where it stands. Valid: anchored with 6 confirmations, no later than prev's spend height + dir_repoint_blocks (an unanchored or late link ends the chain without a read), and its coin pays to the address and cleared the floor at the re-point's own anchor. The claim stands while its current coin is unspent or its spend has fewer than dir_repoint_blocks + 6 confirmations. Every coin read counts toward the coin bound. The cases use the vc24 walk, which walks each claim once; `reads` lists the reads made, in order ('repoint' is the read of a re-point's coin).

cases.name: a re-point in time keeps the handle
cases.why: The coin was spent at S; the re-point is anchored at S + 300, no later than S + dir_repoint_blocks, and moves the claim to the spend's own output, which confirmed at S and so cleared the floor at the re-point's anchor. The claim keeps its place; the later claim is never read.

cases.name: a late re-point loses it
cases.why: Anchored at S + 1009, after the window: ignored without a read. The spend has 2000 confirmations, past dir_repoint_blocks + 6, so the claim is ended and the next one holds.

cases.name: a re-point under a key not bound to the address is ignored
cases.why: The only listing carrying the re-point is signed by a key the address does not bind; the address's state is its bound listing, which carries none. The claim is ended and the next one holds.

cases.name: a re-point too early for its coin ends the chain where it stands
cases.why: At S + 10 the new coin has 11 confirmations, short of dir_floor_confs: that link is invalid, so the claim stays on its spent coin and the link after it is never read. The window has passed, so the next claim holds. A holder in this place publishes a list without the failed link (case 1).

cases.name: inside the window the claim stands with no re-point yet
cases.why: The spend has 500 confirmations, fewer than dir_repoint_blocks + 6: the holder can still re-point, so the claim holds.

cases.name: a chain of two re-points
cases.why: Each re-point is in time for the spend of its prev and its coin clears the floor at its own anchor. The second is read from the coin the first moved to.

cases.name: a re-point cannot rescue a coin that failed the floor at the claim's anchor
cases.why: The claim's own coin confirmed 100 blocks before its anchor: the claim fails for good, and its re-point is never read.

cases.name: a re-point made before the spend
cases.why: Anchored at 925100, before the old coin's spend at 926000, to a coin already aged then: the claim moved before the spend and stands on the new coin.

cases.name: no answer for a re-point's coin before the holder
cases.why: §8.2.5 (4): the walk cannot tell whether the claim moved, so it stops with E_DIR_UNRESOLVED rather than hand the handle on.

cases.name: a re-point to a coin of another address is invalid
cases.why: The new coin pays to another address. With no valid re-point and the window passed, the claim is ended.

cases.name: links after a failed one cost no read
cases.why: Sixteen re-points, all in time; the first pays to another address. The chain ends there after one read: the fifteen after it cost nothing, so junk in a list cannot drain the coin-read bound.

cases.name: a list that does not chain is dropped before any read
cases.why: The second re-point's prev is not the first one's outpoint: the listing is dropped in §8.2.5 (1), Alice's address is never read, and the next claim holds.

cases.name: seventeen re-points are dropped before any read
cases.why: At most 16 re-points per claim (§8.2.9): the listing is dropped in §8.2.5 (1).

notes: Outpoints are synthetic txids; anchors are heights (vc23 shows how a proof gives one).
